chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abd

Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them, said: 'It reached Umm Salama, the wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), that a freedman of hers was disparaging Ali (peace be upon him) and attacking him. So she sent for him, and when he came to her, she said: "O my dear son, it has reached me that you are disparaging Ali and attacking him." He said to her: "Yes, O my mother." She said: "Sit down — may your mother mourn you — until I tell you a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then make your choice. Indeed we were nine women with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and it was my night'

and my day with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). The Prophet entered, beaming with joy, his fingers interlaced with Ali's, his hand placed on him. He said: 'O Umm Salama, leave the house and vacate it for us.' So I left and they turned toward each other, conversing privately. I could hear the sound of their speech but did not know what they were saying, until when midday came, I went to the door and said: 'May I enter, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No.' So I was overcome with a severe fall, from fear that he had sent me away in displeasure, or something had descended from the heavens. Then before long I came to the door

The second time, I said: Shall I enter, O Messenger of God? He said: No. So I was saddened even more intensely than the first time. Then without delay I came to the door a third time, and I said: Shall I enter, O Messenger of God? He said: Enter, O Umm Salama. So I entered, and Ali (peace be upon him) was kneeling before him, saying: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God! If such-and-such were to happen, what do you command me? He said: I command you patience. Then he repeated the question a second time, and he commanded him patience. Then he repeated it a third time, so he said to him: O Ali, O my brother! If that happens from them, then unsheathe your sword and place it on your shoulder,

And strike with it forward again and again until you meet me while your sword is drawn, dripping with their blood. Then he (peace be upon him) turned toward me and said to me: What is this sadness, O Umm Salama? I said: Because of your turning me away, O Messenger of God. So he said to me: By God, I did not turn you away out of anger. Indeed you are upon goodness from God and His Messenger. Rather, you came to me while Jibreel was on my right and Ali was on my left. Jibreel was informing me of the events that will occur after me, and he commanded me to convey that to Ali. O Umm Salama! Listen and bear witness. This is Ali ibn Abi Talib, my brother in this world and my brother in the Hereafter. O Umm Salama! Listen and bear witness. This is Ali ibn Abi Talib, my vizier in this world and my vizier in the Hereafter. O Umm Salama! Listen and bear witness. This is Ali

ibn Abi Talib, the bearer of my banner in this world and the bearer of my banner on the Day of Resurrection. O Umm Salama! Listen and bear witness. This is Ali ibn Abi Talib, my deputy and my vicegerent after me, the fulfiller of my pledges, and the defender of my Pond. O Umm Salama! Listen and bear witness. This is Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Master of the Muslims, the Imam of the God-fearing, the Leader of the bright-faced illuminated ones, and the one who fights the oath-breakers, the unjust, and the apostates. I said: O Messenger of God! Who are the oath-breakers? He said: Those who pledge allegiance to him in Medina and break it in Basra. I said: Who are the unjust? He said: Mu'awiya and his companions from the people of the Levant. I said: Who are the apostates? He said: The people of Nahrawan. So the servant of Umm Salama said: You have relieved me — may God relieve you. By God, I will never insult Ali ever.

key_terms.الذَّائِدُ: Defender, protector, one who wards off
key_terms.النَّاكِثُونَ: Oath-breakers — historically, Talha and Zubayr and their followers at the Battle of the Camel
key_terms.الْحَوْضُ: The Pond (of the Prophet on the Day of Resurrection)
key_terms.الْغُرُّ الْمُحَجَّلُونَ: The radiant ones with bright limbs — believers who will appear with marks of wudu on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.الْقَاسِطُونَ: The deviant/unjust — historically, Mu'awiya and the people of the Levant at the Battle of Siffin
key_terms.الْمَارِقُونَ: The apostates/those who left the religion — historically, the Khawarij at the Battle of Nahrawan
key_terms.فَدَاكَ أَبِي وَأُمِّي: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you — a formula of extreme devotion
key_terms.مُتَهَلِّلٌ: Radiant with joy, beaming with happiness
key_terms.يَتَنَاجَيَانِ: Whispering secretly to one another, holding a private conversation
key_terms.يَتَنَقَّصُ: To belittle, to disparage, to diminish the status of someone

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Ali ibn Abi Talib as his successor and the meaning of the oath-breakers, deviant, and apostates?
ai.summary: Umm Salama, a wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), confronts her servant who had been belittling Imam Ali (AS). She narrates a remarkable event she witnessed: the Prophet, in a private meeting with Ali guided by the archangel Gabriel, gave Ali five solemn proclamations before Umm Salama as witness — naming him his brother, vizier, banner-bearer, successor, and defining his future battles against the oath-breakers (Talha and Zubayr at Basra), the deviant (Mu'awiya at Siffin), and the apostates (Khawarij at Nahrawan). This hadith, transmitted through three Imams (Sadiq, Baqir, Zayn al-Abidin), provides prophetic authority for the legitimacy of Ali's caliphate and his three major wars, and was understood by the early Shia community as a definitive proof of imamate.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi’l Qasim narrated to us from Muhammad b. `Ali al-Sayrafi from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. `Umar from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq

from his father from his grandfather (as). He said: Umm Salama the wife of the Prophet (s) was informed that a servant of hers had lowered the status of `Ali (as) and taunted him. So, she sent for him. When he came to her, she said to him: O my son! I was informed that you lower the status of `Ali and taunt him. He said to her: Yes, mother. She said: Sit – may your mother be bereaved with you – so that I could narrate a hadith to you that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (s). Then, decide for yourself. We were nine women with the Messenger of Allah (s), and it was my night

and my day with the Messenger of Allah (s). So, the Prophet (s) entered, and his fingers were intertwined with the fingers of `Ali – he was placing his hand on him. So, he said: O Umm Salama! Exit the house and leave it for us. So, I left, and they began whispering [to one another]. I heard the discussion, but I could not make out what they were saying. When it became midday, I went to the door, and I said: Shall I enter, O Messenger of Allah? He said: No. I was saddened, fearing that he had turned me away out of anger, or that something had been revealed from heaven. I did not remain except that I came to the door

a second time, and I said: Shall I enter, O Messenger of Allah? So, he said: No. So, I became even more saddened than the first time. Then, I did not remain except that I came to the door a third time, and I said: Shall I enter, O Messenger of Allah? So, he said: Enter, Umm Salama. So, I entered, and `Ali (as) was kneeling in front of him, saying: May my mother and my father be your sacrifice, O Messenger of Allah! If such-and-such were to happen, then what do you command me to do? He said: I command you to be patient. Then, he repeated the saying a second time, and he commanded him to be patient. Then, he repeated the saying a third time, so he said to him: O `Ali, O my brother! If they do that, then unsheathe your sword, place it on your shoulders,

and strike before you again and again until you meet me and your sword is dripping in their blood. Then, he (as) turned to me and said to me: Why are you sad, Umm Salama? I said: Because you were turning me away, O Messenger of Allah. So, he said to me: By Allah, I did not turn you away out of anger. Surely, you are upon goodness from Allah and His Messenger. Rather, you came to me while Gabriel was on my right and `Ali was on my left. Gabriel was informing me of what will occur after me, and he commanded me to impart that to `Ali. O Umm Salama! Listen and bear witness. This `Ali b. Abi Talib is my brother in this world and my brother in the Hereafter. O Umm Salama! Listen and bear witness. This `Ali b. Abi Talib is my vizier in this world and my vizier in the Hereafter. O Umm Salama! Listen and bear witness. This `Ali

b. Abi Talib is the one that holds my banner in this world and the one who will hold my banner anon in the Resurrection. O Umm Salama! Listen and bear witness. This `Ali b. Abi Talib is my deputy and my vicegerent (khalifa) after me. He is my judge of my articles and the defender of my Pond. O Umm Salama! Listen and bear witness. This `Ali b. Abi Talib is the Master of the Muslims, the Imam of the Godfearing, the Leader of the shining believers, and the killer of the oath breakers, the deviators, and the apostates. I said: O Messenger of Allah! Who are the oath breakers? He said: Those who pledge allegiance to him in Medina and betray him in Basra. I said: Who are the deviators? He said: Mu`awiya and his companions from the people of the Levant. I said: Who are the apostates? He said: The people of Nahrawan. So, the servant of Umm Salama said: You have relieved me, may Allah relieve you. By Allah, I will never insult `Ali.
